title: How Cats Talk
question: How do cats talk?
coverAlt: Big and Little Wonderer: How Cats Talk
readAloud: Big Wonderer and Little Wonderer watch two cats meet in a sunny window. One cat walks closer with its tail held high.
Cats talk with sounds and with their bodies. A meow may ask for food, company, or an open door. A quick mrrp can be a friendly hello.

readAloud.ask: Can you point to the cat saying hello with its tail?

readAloud: A purr often comes when a cat feels cozy, but a worried cat may purr too. We look at the whole cat for clues.
One cat turns its ears sideways.
Cats may hiss when they need more space. We stay back and let the cat choose.

readAloud.ask: Can you make your arm into a high hello tail?

readAloud: The cats rest on a pillow and slowly close their eyes. A slow blink can say, “I trust you.” Then one rubs its cheek on a chair leg, leaving a familiar scent.

readAloud.ask: What cat message would you like to copy?

readAloud: Big Wonderer and Little Wonderer slow-blink from a calm distance. Cats talk with sounds, tails, ears, eyes, and smells.
steps: Read the story aloud together and stop at each “Ask”.
Print the pack and pick two or three pages; there is no need to do them all.
Point, circle, trace and color. Snip only with a grown-up.
Fold the picture book and read it again at bedtime.
why: Listening to how cats talk helps your child notice sounds and body signals while practicing counting, letter sounds and tracing.
